requested.title: sanitizeHtml allowlists start tags only — unmatched end tags are never inspected
htmlToText silently discards all remaining text after a void element in its skip list
/hn redirect built from client-controlled req.url instead of the configured proxy.origin
/hn is a raw Bun route value, so it bypasses the entire Mochi request pipeline and double-redirects
fetchUser and fetchStoryIds proxy an uncached third-party API call per request with no rate limiting
fetchItem memoizes upstream failures as "item not found" for up to 10 minutes
itemCache has only age-based eviction, so id enumeration grows it without bound
`COPY . .` bakes the project's `.env` (MOCHI_KEY and all other secrets) into the image because the shipped `.dockerignore` omits `.env*`
Template image has no `USER` directive, so the scaffolded app runs as root — unlike every other Dockerfile in the repo

parsedVerdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism is now CONFIRMED rather than speculative — stronger than the finding's own 'low' confidence. Three independent sources agree there is no document-level end-tag handler (bun-types/html-rewriter.d.ts `HTMLRewriterDocumentContentHandlers` exposes only doctype/comments/text/end; workerd's `DocumentContentHandlers` matches; the Cloudflare docs source lists the same four), so end tags are observable only through `Element.onEndTag`, which requires the start tag to have matched first — an orphan `` is structurally unobservable through the entire public API. And lol-html does pass it through: its selector stack explicitly early-returns on a stray name (`if !self.open_name_counts.contains_key(&local_name) { return; }`, with the comment 'reject a stray end tag in O(1)'), so nothing matches, the removed-content counter stays 0, `emission_enabled` stays true, and `flush_remaining_input` writes the bytes verbatim. lol-html is a streaming tokenizer with only a partial tree-builder simulator — it runs html5lib's tokenizer suite but no tree-construction suite, keeps no stack of open HTML elements for end-tag matching, and its own test passes a bogus `` straight through, which HTML5 tree construction would discard. So `sanitizeHtml('x')` would indeed return `x`. My verdict nonetheless rests on reachability, which the finding never establishes and which is independent of all of the above. `sanitizeHtml` has exactly three call sites, all HN API fields: `comment.text` (HNComments.svelte:22), `item.text` (HNItem.svelte:40), `user.about` (HNUser.svelte:36). The attacker's only channel is posting to Hacker News, and HN permits no raw HTML in user content — it entity-escapes `<`/`>` and emits only its own `

`/``/``/`

`, every tag of which is already allowlisted; its unbalanced output is unclosed *start* tags (`
` as a separator), not orphan end tags. The repo's own fixture corroborates the escaping aggressiveness: hn-sanitize.test.ts:182 shows HN emitting `/` for a plain `/` inside its own href. Influencing the response any other way means breaking TLS to hacker-news.firebaseio.com or compromising HN itself. Second, the impact ceiling is capped regardless: lines 32-48 strip every attribute except `a[href]`, which is entity-decoded then re-serialized through `new URL()` with an http(s)-only check, and output lands in ordinary `
` content — so a leaked end tag yields DOM restructuring, never an attribute, style, handler or script. Not exploitable today; worth fixing as hardening, since the whole argument collapses if this helper is ever pointed at a source that does not pre-escape.

Confirmed as a real defect, but the finding's PRIMARY failure mode is wrong and its parenthetical alternative is what actually happens. I traced the whole chain: lol-html's `Element::on_end_tag` returns `Err` when `can_have_content()` is false; the C API that Bun links does `element.end_tag_handlers().ok_or("No end tag.")` and returns -1; `lol_html.h` documents it explicitly ('Not all elements (for example, `
`) support end tags. If this function is called on such an element, this function returns an error code'); Bun's Zig wrapper maps `-1 => error.Fail`; and Bun's JS binding does NOT swallow it — it calls `globalObject.throwValue(err)`, producing an `Error` with `name: "HTMLRewriterError"` and message `"No end tag."`. So `htmlToText('tail')` does not return `''` — it THROWS synchronously out of `transform(string)`, which for SSR at HNItem.svelte:11 and HNStoryRow.svelte:7-8 falls through to the route handler and renders the error page as a 500. That is a worse consequence than described, and the finding did anticipate it in its parenthetical ('broken either way'). The underlying premise is certain: `canHaveContent` is documented 'false for void elements like
', `embed` is void, and the line 63 decrement can therefore never be reached. The decisive evidence that this is a real divergence rather than theory is the framework's own copies of the identical idiom: `email/mailer.ts:27` skips only 'script, style' (no void element) and `utils/index.ts:215-221` applies the counter only to ``/``, with utils/index.test.ts:126 explicitly pinning 'the onEndTag depth-counter invariant' — the demo copy widened the selector to include `embed` and broke it. The finding's stuck-counter mechanism is also genuinely reachable, just via a different trigger: `onEndTag` is documented not to fire for implicitly-closed elements, so an unclosed `

Mechanism verified. `new URL('/hn/front', req.url)` takes its authority and scheme from the raw Bun request, and the framework exists specifically to avoid that: runtime/proxy.ts documents `buildPublicUrl()` as the thing 'every per-request handler in Mochi.ts uses… so event.url, internal redirects, and the CSRF check all see the public origin under a TLS-terminating reverse proxy', and `proxy.origin` as what 'drives event.url.origin, internal redirects such as trailing-slash canonicalisation'. Being a raw Bun route value (see F4), this route gets none of it, even though demos/src/index.ts:27 configures `proxy.origin` precisely for this. The downgrade half is the solid half, and it sits on the documented entry path — worse than the finding claims: packages/docs/200-demos.md:12 links readers to `https://demos.mochi.fast/hn`, and packages/demos/src/Landing.svelte:23 links `/hn/` (raw route values are mirrored onto both slash forms at Mochi.ts:1546-1551). build.yml:49-57 deploys demos via CapRover on the plain-HTTP root Dockerfile with no `tls` in `Mochi.serve()`, so `req.url` is always `http://…` and every HTTPS visitor to that link receives `Location: http://demos.mochi.fast/hn/front`; my greps of packages/demos, packages/site/src, packages/mochi/src and packages/minimal for `strict-transport`/`hsts` returned nothing, so no in-repo HSTS blunts it. Two bounds on severity: the Host-reflection half is largely blocked in the deployed topology, since CapRover's nginx selects the app by `server_name`, so `Host: evil.tld` never reaches this container (it stays valid for direct container access or non-vhost-routed deployments); and nothing in packages/demos/src sets a cookie (grep for `cookies.set`/`Set-Cookie` is empty), so the cleartext hop carries no credentials. The 'open-redirect' slug is a misnomer — the path is fixed and the Host is echoed to the host the client asked for — but the underlying defect (origin derived from the request rather than `proxy.origin`) is exactly as described, and packages/site/src/index.ts:56 using `event.url` for the same pattern is the right in-repo contrast. Residual real risk: an sslstrip-able plaintext round trip on the demo's main entry point.

Verified end-to-end in the framework. All five `isMochi*` guards begin with `typeof value === 'object'` (types.ts:53, 88, 100, 237, 255), so a bare arrow function fails every one; `registerRoutePattern` returns null and Mochi.ts:1537 falls through to `bunRoutes[pattern] = handler as BunRouteValue`, with the adjacent comment confirming 'Raw Bun route values (static Responses, HTML imports) answer on both slash forms' and lines 1546-1551 doing the mirroring. Because the value is assigned straight into `bunRoutes`, it never passes through `wrapRequest` (called only at Mochi.ts:1012 and 1028, inside the page branch), so there is no request context, no CSRF, no rate-limit check, no cookie finalization, no `handle` middleware, and no `mochiEvents.emit('request', …)` — the observability hole is the most concrete consequence, since the route is simply absent from `consoleLogger()` output. The double redirect is real and on the primary in-app path: Landing.svelte:23 links `/hn/`, the mirrored raw route answers it and returns `Location: /hn/front` without a slash, and `trailingSlash: 'always'` redirects again. One factual correction: `trailingSlashRedirect`'s `permanentRedirect` (runtime/trailingSlash.ts) issues **301** for GET/HEAD and 308 only for other methods, so a browser's second hop is a 301, not the 308 stated. The practical security impact of the listed bypasses is nil for this specific route — demos configures no global `rateLimit` (grep of index.ts is empty), the route sets no cookies, and CSRF is irrelevant to a GET redirect — which is why BUG rather than a security severity is right. I deliberately did not collapse this into F3: although both anchor on line 5, they are distinct defects with distinct root causes (F3 is which URL you read; F4 is which route kind you register) and either would survive fixing the other.

Every factual claim checks out. `fetchItem` (hn-api.ts:33-45) validates with `Number.isSafeInteger(id) && id > 0` and funnels through `itemCache`, with the comment stating the intent; `fetchUser` (47-53) and `fetchStoryIds` (55-61) do neither. `/hn/user/:id` is a public `Mochi.page` (routes.ts:12) and `params.id` reaches `fetchUser` unvalidated at HNUser.svelte:10. The double fetch is confirmed: HNUser.svelte:40 renders `<HNRecentSubmissions mochi:defer userId={user.id}>` and HNRecentSubmissions.svelte:9 calls `fetchUser(userId)` again purely to re-read `submitted`, which the page already holds. `fetchStories` -> `fetchStoryIds` runs uncached on every render of `/hn/front|new|ask|show|jobs`, which are the nav targets at HNLayout.svelte:25-31, so the ~500-id array is re-pulled from Firebase per request. And there is no abuse control anywhere: my grep of packages/demos/src for `rateLimit|protection|captcha` returns zero hits and `Mochi.serve()` sets none, even though commit 1289d8f8 established the pattern of adding per-route limits to demo routes. I would temper one phrase: at 1 attacker request -> 1-2 upstream requests this is not really an 'amplifier', so the credible harm is the server's IP being throttled or blocked by hacker-news.firebaseio.com (degrading the demo for everyone) plus per-request latency pinned to an uncached third-party call, not bandwidth amplification. I independently confirmed the finding's own disclaimer that this is not SSRF: `encodeURIComponent` percent-encodes `/ ? # :` and `BASE` is a module constant, and a `..` segment cannot traverse because `${BASE}/user/${'..'}.json` yields the single segment `...json`. Real, worth fixing, MEDIUM is fair.

Traced through the cache implementation and confirmed exactly. `fetchItem`'s `!res.ok -> return null` sits inside the `itemCache.fetch` callback, and `MochiCache.run` persists whatever `fn()` resolves to by writing `this.serialize({ value, createdAt: this.now() })`, where `serialize` defaults to `identity` (cache.ts:~113). `MemoryStorage.setItem` then stores `{ value: {value: null, createdAt}, writtenAt }`, so `getItem` returns a truthy object, `read()`'s `raw == null ? null : …` yields a non-null entry, and `lookup`'s only miss test is `if (entry == null)` (cache.ts:141) — a stored `value: null` is a bona fide cache hit. The timing claims hold too: `age < minTimeToStale` (60s) returns 'fresh' with no revalidation attempted at all, and between 60s and `maxTimeToLive` (600s) the stale null is served while a background `run` refreshes. The recommendation is sound because `run` reaches `storage.setItem` only after `await fn()` resolves, so a thrown error is genuinely never memoized. The conflation identified is real: Firebase answers 200 + JSON `null` for an unknown id, which should be cached, and this code makes a transient 429/503 indistinguishable from it. One small imprecision to note: a transport-level failure (a rejected `fetch`) already propagates and is not cached, so only HTTP-status failures get memoized. The secondary claim also holds — `fetchStoryIds` casts `res.json()` with no shape check, so a 200 plus a non-array body (including JSON `null`) makes `fetchStories`' `ids.slice` throw a TypeError into a 500 at hn-api.ts:66.

Verified, and the deployed configuration is actually worse than the finding assumes. `MemoryStorage` (cache/cache-storage.ts) is a plain `Map` whose only eviction is `sweep()` deleting entries where `now - writtenAt > maxAge`; its options are just `maxAge`/`purgeInterval`, with no `maxEntries` or byte cap anywhere — so the mitigation added by 1289d8f8 bounds age, not count, and that commit's own message frames the fix as exactly 'MemoryStorage({ maxAge: 600_000, purgeInterval: 60_000 })'. `/hn/item/:id` is public (routes.ts:11) and `fetchItem` accepts any safe positive integer, so id walking inserts one distinct `item:<id>` key per request with nothing capping the count, and packages/demos/src configures no rate limit at all. The memory-pressure analysis is accurate — `MemoryStorage`'s constructor calls `registerPressureResponder`, `respondToPressure('critical')` calls `clear()`, Linux reports only 'critical', and memoryPressure.ts carries the verbatim comment 'the OS signal never fires on a healthy Linux box' — but I found the backstop is not even installed here: Mochi.ts:2071 guards it with `if (!development && (options.memoryPressure ?? true))`, and build.yml deploys demos on the dev-mode root Dockerfile, whose line 5 states that `bun run dev:<workspace>` sets NODE_ENV=development, so `development` is true and `installMemoryPressureHandler()` is skipped entirely. The finding's cache-key observation is correct and fairly conceded: the id is integer-validated before interpolation, so there is no key poisoning. The one imprecision is the title — growth is bounded by (insert rate x 600s) rather than literally unbounded, though the body says so correctly — but the requested hard entry-count ceiling is the right ask, and MEDIUM is appropriate for a memory-exhaustion path on a deployed public route with no rate limit.

Every link in the chain verified. packages/cli/src/templates.ts:14-27 points the `minimal` template at `khromov/mochi/packages/minimal` with no `#ref`, so download.ts:15's `const [pathPart = '', ref = 'HEAD']` resolves to the live default branch; `extractTemplate()` (download.ts:33-46) globs the subdir and writes every match with `Bun.write`, with no filter, allowlist or exclusion anywhere in cli.ts/create.ts/download.ts/utils.ts; and download.test.ts:58-59 asserts `.gitignore` survives extraction. I confirmed this empirically rather than by inference: cli-tests/mochi-test-1785454573-minimal/ is a real scaffold output containing both `.dockerignore` and a `Dockerfile` byte-identical to the template apart from the then-current base tag. packages/minimal/.dockerignore is six lines (node_modules, .git, .mochi, Dockerfile, .dockerignore, *.log) with no `.env*`, while line 8's `COPY . .` sits in a single-stage build, so anything matched persists in the final image layer. The secret source is the documented path: packages/mochi/src/cli/generateKey.ts:29-34 resolves `path.resolve(cwd, '.env')` and writes `MOCHI_KEY=…`, documented at packages/docs/183-cli.md:88, and Bun auto-loads `.env`. Two pieces of evidence make this an oversight rather than a trade-off: the root .dockerignore:8 does list `.env*`, and packages/docs/185-docker.md:48-53 prints a recommended `.dockerignore` that includes `.env*` — the shipped template contradicts the project's own documentation. The `.gitignore` compounding claim also checks out: `ensureGitignore()` (utils.ts:196-203) returns early when the file exists, so DEFAULT_GITIGNORE's `.env`/`.env.local` (utils.ts:190-191) never reach a scaffold, and packages/demos/.gitignore has the same gap. The caveat that keeps this at MEDIUM is correctly stated in the finding: create-mochi does not itself create a `.env` (minimal references MOCHI_KEY nowhere), so the user must put a secret there and then build/distribute the image — routine given the docs, but a required precondition.

Confirmed as a factual deviation from the project's own baseline. packages/minimal/Dockerfile is 13 lines, single-stage, with no `USER` and no `HEALTHCHECK`, so `CMD ["bun", "run", "start"]` at line 13 runs as uid 0. The claim that `oven/bun` defaults to root is independently supported from inside this repo: Dockerfile.production runs `RUN apk add --no-cache ncdu` (root-only) before switching at line 107, and all four other Dockerfiles explicitly switch — root Dockerfile:70, Dockerfile.production:107, packages/demos/Dockerfile.production:63, Dockerfile.memtest:57 — which would be pointless if `bun` were already the default user. The production files also go to real trouble to support the drop (`chown -R bun:bun` on `.mochi`/`src`, `/data/image-cache`), reinforcing that the template's omission is an oversight rather than a decision. Because the template ships verbatim through create-mochi (chain verified under F8), every `--template minimal` scaffold inherits it. I agree with the finding's own framing that this is defense-in-depth rather than directly exploitable: it needs a separate code-execution primitive before root matters, at which point the consequences are write access to /app source and node_modules (a backdoor that persists across restarts on a volume-backed mount), a wider syscall surface for escape attempts, and root-owned files on bind mounts. One correction to the recommendation's aside: the 'add a HEALTHCHECK like the other Dockerfiles' point is only partly supported, since packages/demos/Dockerfile.production has none either — though packages/minimal/src/index.ts:15 does serve `/health`, so the probe would work. MEDIUM is a touch generous for a pure hardening gap, but with no lower security tier available I am leaving it unchanged.
